scope: Ruby and PHP shared definitions, independent examples, verified acquisition, runtime compatibility, managed environments, quality gates and relocated releases

native_acquisition.unix: Ruby source SHA-256 and PHP source SHA-256 plus pinned OpenPGP signatures passed actual Linux x64 builds. Private images activate after successful builds. Source-build cache paths include the host OS identity.
native_acquisition.ruby_windows: All three pinned x64 archives passed recorded SHA-256 and signatures by the pinned official AppVeyor key. The real 4.0.7 archive passed bounded 7-Zip preflight and extraction: 18,253 files, 276,090,150 extracted bytes. Windows executables were not run.
native_acquisition.bootstrap: Actual Bundler, Composer and Xdebug acquisitions passed SHA-256. Composer also passed its detached signature. Absent upstream authentication is recorded in metadata and trust documentation.

composer: verified archive and replayed cache-hit event accepted without catalog mutation
bootstrap: incorrect Bundler and Composer versions rejected
failed Bundler installation cleans staging and permits retry
archive: path escapes, links, duplicates, encryption and excessive resource claims rejected

cache_verification.ruby: Installed gems and Bundler extension caches include the runtime installation identity. Actual Debian Dev Container gates passed after eliminating cross-SDK extension reuse.
cache_verification.php: Xdebug caches use PHP executable/configuration and acquisition identity. Startup filtering excludes tooling from branch collection.

skills.ruby-dependency-refresh: quick_validate passed; canonical .agents and .claude discovery links resolve
skills.php-dependency-refresh: quick_validate passed; canonical .agents and .claude discovery links resolve

limitations: Hosted CI, macOS arm64, Windows x64 and Linux arm64 execution remain workbench:TSK-7.
Unix native runtimes compile once using the host SDK, then reuse external caches.
Existing Nix and Guix input revisions were retained.
No commit, push, publication or ADR acceptance occurred; draft ADR-1B and ADR-1C require human review.
